{{Short description|American mathematician (born 1954)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Dennis M. DeTurck''' (born July 15, 1954) is an American mathematician known for his work in [[partial differential equation]]s and [[Riemannian geometry]], in particular contributions to the theory of the [[Ricci flow]] and the [[prescribed Ricci curvature problem]]. He first used the DeTurck trick to give an alternative proof of the short time existence of the Ricci flow, which has found other uses since then.

== Education ==
DeTurck received a B.S. (1976) from [[Drexel University]]. He received an M.A. (1978) and Ph.D. (1980) in mathematics from the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. His Ph.D. supervisor was [[Jerry Kazdan]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=23121}}</ref>

== Career ==
DeTurck is currently Robert A. Fox Leadership Professor and Professor of Mathematics at the University of Pennsylvania, where he was the Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences from 2005 to 2017 and Faculty Director of [[University of Pennsylvania College Houses#Riepe College House|Riepe College House]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://riepe.house.upenn.edu/house_staff|title=House Staff, Riepe College House, U. of Penn.|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114051058/http://riepe.house.upenn.edu/house_staff|archive-date=2012-11-14}}</ref> from 2009 to 2018. In 2002, DeTurck won the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]] from the [[Mathematical Association of America]] for his teaching.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/haimo-award-distinguished-teaching|title=Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award|date=2007-04-10|publisher=[[The Mathematical Association of America]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190507072419/https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/haimo-award-distinguished-teaching|archive-date=2019-05-07|url-status=live|access-date=2007-12-26}}</ref> Despite being recognized for excellence in teaching, he has been criticized for his belief that fractions are "as obsolete as Roman numerals" and suggesting that they not be taught to younger students.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.delawareonline.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20071226/NEWS03/712260337/1006/NEWS|title=Educators divided by fractions debate|author=Milford|first=Maureen|date=2007-12-26|work=[[The News Journal]]|access-date=2007-12-26|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130408055104/http://www.delawareonline.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20071226/NEWS03/712260337/1006/NEWS&nclick_check=1|archive-date=2013-04-08|location=Philadelphia|quote=A few years ago, Dennis DeTurck, an award-winning professor of mathematics at the University of Pennsylvania, stood at an outdoor podium on campus and proclaimed "Down with fractions!"|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In January 2012, he shared the [[Chauvenet Prize]] with three mathematical collaborators.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://penntoday.upenn.edu/news/penn-mathematicians-win-2012-chauvenet-prize|title=Penn Mathematicians Win 2012 Chauvenet Prize|last=Baillie|first=Katherine Unger|date=January 30, 2012|work=Penn Today|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190530215408/https://penntoday.upenn.edu/news/penn-mathematicians-win-2012-chauvenet-prize|archive-date=May 30, 2019|url-status=live|publisher=University of Pennsylvania}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=DeTurck, Dennis|author2=Gluck, Herman|author3=Pomerleano, Daniel|author4=Vela-Vick, Shea|title=The Four Vertex Theorem and Its Converse|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=54|year=2007|issue=2|pages=192–207|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/the-four-vertex-theorem-and-its-converse|archive-date=September 8, 2016|access-date=February 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160908202815/http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/the-four-vertex-theorem-and-its-converse|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>
